help.article.gettingStarted.content:
Welcome to AnkiTov!

AnkiTov helps you manage spaced repetition practice for your students.

First Steps

  1. Upload flashcard decks in Setup → Decks
  2. Create classes in Setup → Classes
  3. Create Practice Plans in Setup → Practice Plans
  4. Generate practice sessions in Classroom → Study Session
  5. Monitor progress on the Dashboard
help.article.practicePlans.content:
What is a Practice Plan?

A Practice Plan tells AnkiTov which topics a student should review and how often per week.

How to Create a Plan

  1. Go to Setup → Practice Plans
  2. Click ＋ New Plan
  3. Choose which modules (topics) to include
  4. Set the Weekly Sessions number (most teachers use 3)
  5. Assign the plan to students
💡 Tip: Start with 3 weekly sessions per student.
help.article.modules.content:
Modules = Topic Areas

A module is a collection of related flashcards — like "Fractions", "Vocabulary", or "Cell Biology". Each Practice Plan combines one or more modules.

Managing Modules

Go to Setup → Tracks & Profiles to see all available modules.
help.article.sessions.content:
What is a Practice Session?

A practice session is a personalized set of review cards for one student to complete in one sitting.

How to Generate

  1. Go to Classroom → Study Session
  2. Pick a student (or multiple students)
  3. Choose their Practice Plan
  4. Set session duration if needed
  5. Click Generate
help.article.classes.content:
Classes

Classes let you group students for easier management. Filter the Dashboard, Insights, and Progress views by class.

How to Get Started

  1. Go to Setup → Classes
  2. Click ＋ Create a Class
  3. Add students by importing from your profiles folder or a CSV file
  4. Assign Practice Plans and decks to the whole class
help.article.decks.content:
Decks

Decks are collections of flashcards your students practice from. Upload .apkg files and distribute them to classes or individual students.

Upload & Distribute

  1. Go to Setup → Decks
  2. Click ＋ Upload or drag-drop an .apkg file
  3. Click Distribute on a deck to send it to students
help.article.progress.content:
Progress (Compliance)

Progress shows how consistently each student is completing their assigned practice sessions.

Color Codes

  • 🟢 Green (80–100%): On track — great job!
  • 🟡 Yellow (50–79%): Slightly behind — may need a reminder
  • 🔴 Red (below 50%): At risk — needs attention
help.article.insights.content:
Class Insights

Insights shows class-wide trends: retention curves, common problem areas, and practice patterns.

Select a class from the dropdown to see data for that group.
help.article.terminology.content:
Teacher Terms → What They Mean

You seeWhat it means
ModuleA topic area like "Fractions" or "Vocabulary"
Practice PlanA set of modules + a weekly session target
Practice SessionA personalized review set for one sitting
Weekly SessionsHow many practice sessions per week (1–7)
ProgressHow consistently a student is practicing
RetentionPercent of cards remembered correctly
At-RiskStudents who missed 2+ sessions this week
help.article.sync.content:
Sync Dashboard

The Sync screen shows whether each student's practice data is synchronized. Green means up to date; red means sync is needed or has failed.

Click Trigger Full Sync to force-sync all students at once.
help.article.faq.content:
FAQ

What's the difference between a Module and a Practice Plan?

A Module is a topic area (e.g., "Fractions"). A Practice Plan combines one or more modules with a weekly session target.

How often should students practice?

Start with 3 sessions per week. Adjust based on progress data.

Can a student have multiple Practice Plans?

No — each student has one active plan at a time. Assigning a new plan replaces the old one.
